icloud.howTo: How to create an app-specific password
icloud.step1: Go to <link>appleid.apple.com</link> and sign in with your Apple ID.
icloud.step2: Choose Sign-In and Security and then App-Specific Passwords.
icloud.step3: Create a new password, for example named "{brand}", and paste it below.
icloud.why: Why? Apple does not allow other services to sign in with your regular password. You can revoke an app-specific password at any time at appleid.apple.com. It requires that you have turned on two-factor authentication. {brand} only reads your calendars and never writes to them.

icloud.disconnectDescription: {brand} deletes the stored app-specific password and the fetched iCloud events. Your time entries remain. Remember to also revoke the password at appleid.apple.com.

outlook.title: Outlook calendar
outlook.intro: Do you keep your calendar in Outlook or Microsoft 365? See your meetings in {brand} and track time from them.
outlook.readOnlyNote: {brand} only asks to read your calendars and never writes to them. You sign in with Microsoft, and {brand} never sees your password.
outlook.brokenConnection: The connection to Outlook no longer works
outlook.disconnectDescription: {brand} deletes the stored access keys and the fetched Outlook events. Your time entries stay. You can also remove {brand} under apps with access in your Microsoft account.
